prompt:
**Setting ("Calculators Made In Mellon College").** Every day, customers bring orders $(d_i,q_i,p_i)$: $d_i=1$ or $d_i=-1$ indicates the direction of the order (the officers sell to, or buy from, the customer), $q_i\le1000$ is the quantity and $p_i\le200$ is the price per calculator. The officers must fill an order entirely or not at all, and want to end the day with no calculators in inventory. Given a list of $n$ tuples $(d_i,q_i,p_i)$, find a subset $S\subseteq[n]$ that maximizes $\sum_{i\in S}d_iq_ip_i$ subject to $\sum_{i\in S}d_iq_i=0$.

For example, for the eight orders $(-1,4,41)$, $(1,5,44)$, $(1,3,45)$, $(1,100,40)$, $(1,11,43)$, $(-1,95,48)$, $(-1,3,43)$, $(-1,12,38)$ the maximum is $79$.

Give an algorithm that solves the problem in time $O(n^2)$ (treating the bounds on $q_i$ and $p_i$ as constants), and explain why it is correct and why it runs in that time.
answer: A dynamic program over the running quantity balance $b=\sum d_iq_i$, which lies in $[-1000n,1000n]$, runs in $O(1000\,n\cdot n)=O(n^2)$; the example evaluates to $79$.

solutions.title: Dynamic programming over the balance
solutions.body:
Let $f_j(b)$ be the maximum value of $\sum d_iq_ip_i$ over subsets of the first $j$ orders whose quantities satisfy $\sum d_iq_i=b$ (and $-\infty$ if there is none). Then $f_0(0)=0$, $f_0(b)=-\infty$ otherwise, and
$$f_j(b)=\max\bigl(f_{j-1}(b),\ f_{j-1}(b-d_jq_j)+d_jq_jp_j\bigr).$$
The answer is $f_n(0)$ (the empty subset gives $0$, so the answer is never negative). A standard reconstruction pointer recovers the subset.

*Correctness:* every subset either omits order $j$ or contains it; in the second case the rest has balance $b-d_jq_j$ and the profit splits additively, so the recurrence is exact.

*Running time:* the balance after $j$ orders lies in $[-1000j,1000j]$, so each layer has at most $2000n+1$ states, each computed in $O(1)$. Over $n$ layers that is $O(2000\,n^2)=O(n^2)$ operations. (The naive $O(2^n)$ solution enumerates all subsets.)

*Example:* running the recurrence on the eight given orders gives $f_8(0)=79$, matching the stated maximum (checked also by brute force over all $2^8$ subsets).

reviewNote: No official solution exists for the TCS round; the algorithm was written by us and tested against brute force.
